transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-04-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (VertexLynx CTO), Maya Singh (Platform Lead), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Sofia Alvarez (Security)

Auto-generated Summary: Technical packaging/certification handoff for VertexLynx offline deploy offering. Multiple action items captured.

00:00 - Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we planned this as the packaging and handoff for the offline deploy, uh, marketplace listing. we wanted to make sure packaging, kvm — k m s integration, and test/benchmarks are aligned.
02:12 - Daniel Park: thanks, ava. quick context — we are trying to ship a private/airgapped offering for enterprise customers, want the vendor listing in cloud-marketplaces but need the offline bundle certified for our install teams. main constraints: customer ops wants simple helm chart, small image sizes, and KMS compatibility with our HSM.
04:05 - Carlos Mendes: okay makes sense. when you say small image sizes, are we talking quantized model bundles only or the entire runtime? because redwood runtime has a few flavors, there’s the full GPU runtime and a quantized CPU path — sometimes transcribed as, uh, 'red-wood dedicated' on docs —
05:00 - Maya Singh: mostly quantized, ideally q4 or int8 variants. but we also want a fallback path that runs on GPU nodes in their datacenter. so two flavors: offline quantized bundle for small customers, and full GPU container for larger installs.
06:40 - Priya Nair: noted. for the quant path we need to validate model quality vs QPS. can you share typical seq lengths and percentile distributions? that impacts our batching and kernel selection for the offline build.
08:15 - Liam O'Connor: typical seq len is 256 tokens median, 512 at 95th. p50 latency target for quantized path is 120ms per response for 256 seq with batching up to 4.
09:20 - Carlos Mendes: okay that helps. latency target may be tight on CPU quantized at that seq len — we'll run a bench but might recommend increasing the p50 to 150ms unless you can accept smaller batches.
11:05 - Sofia Alvarez: on security, we need to confirm KMS/HSM flow. we use a YubiHSM and HashiCorp vault in our labs. how does Redwood expect key rotation, and can the bundle integrate with our KMS via kms-plugin?
12:30 - Ava Chen: we support KMS integrations via our connector; in private mode the control plane is customer-managed and keys can be brought-your-own. i'll attach our KMS integration guide. note: sometimes the doc auto-transcribes 'KMS' weirdly.
14:00 - Daniel Park: perfect. also compliance: we need audit log hooks, and the package should emit structured events to a syslog or fluentd endpoint.
15:24 - Priya Nair: runtime already includes audit hooks; we ship a sidecar for fluentd forwarding in the helm chart. we'll add an example filter to redact PII — though that's part of the ops playbook.
17:05 - Maya Singh: what about SSO for the management console? we expect SAML/SSO for the installer UI and RBAC for operators.
18:30 - Carlos Mendes: for private deployments, console is optional; we provide a minimal control plane package that can be deployed behind SSO. we will produce instructions for SAML metadata and OIDC connectors.
20:10 - Liam O'Connor: integration with our OPA gate is a hard requirement — the deploy must expose admission hooks so our pipeline can enforce policies before enabling the runtime.
21:35 - Priya Nair: yes, helm chart will include admission webhook configs. we need to confirm which APIs you want gated — we can default to model-upload and rollout APIs.
23:00 - Daniel Park: regarding marketplace listing, what artifacts do you need? we have a marketplace team but not familiar with Redwood-specific packaging.
24:12 - Ava Chen: we need a signed artifact bundle, container images in tarball form, helm chart with values.yaml examples, a marketplace manifest, and a certification checklist. i'll send the checklist and an example manifest.
26:02 - Maya Singh: what about images — do you prefer OCI tarballs or raw containerd bundles? some airgapped customers require specific formats.
27:45 - Carlos Mendes: we can produce both. default is OCI tarball; if you need containerd or cri-o bundles we can add that to the packaging pipeline.
29:10 - Sofia Alvarez: who owns CVE scanning during the cert? we run our own SCA but want to avoid duplicated effort.
30:25 - Priya Nair: we can publish SBOMs for every image and provide the scanning outputs from our CI. you'll still want to run your internal SCA but SBOM + signed attestations should speed things up.
32:00 - Daniel Park: thanks, that helps. bench plan? we mentioned runbook and a test dataset.
33:15 - Carlos Mendes: we'll run three lab profiles: functional (correctness/quality), perf (latency/p50/p95 with your data distribution), and scale (concurrent clients, autoscaling behavior). we'll share the runbook and a script to replay workloads — it's the same harness we use for dedicated acceptance.
35:00 - Maya Singh: regarding quantization, can you confirm if payload post-processing (structured outputs) is preserved? occasionally tokenization differences make downstream eval flaky.
36:20 - Priya Nair: tokenization is consistent if you use the same tokenizer version. we'll package the tokenizer binaries in the bundle and pin versions in the manifest to prevent drift.
38:00 - Liam O'Connor: on logging levels, for UAT we want debug, but production must default to info and redact PII. can this be a helm value?
39:22 - Carlos Mendes: yes, logLevel is a chart value and we can include a 'pii_redaction' toggle that wraps the fluentd filter.
41:05 - Daniel Park: timeline — certification for marketplace expected end of May ideally. is that realistic?
42:30 - Ava Chen: if we start the lab run week of 2027-05-10 and your team provisions the VPC before 2027-05-05, we can complete perf and security checks by end of May; compliance review may push into early June depending on SOC2 artifacts.
44:10 - Sofia Alvarez: we'll share SOC2 summary and a list of in-scope controls by 2027-05-08.
46:00 - Maya Singh: also, can we discuss licensing model for offline bundles? we need to understand metering and offline usage reporting options.
47:28 - Priya Nair: there are a few options: license file with heartbeat to your ops, periodic usage reports you can ingest, or a completely offline flat-fee. we'll include options in the pricing appendix.
49:05 - Daniel Park: for POC we want a 30-day pilot with a single cluster and 3 seats. can that be done without marketplace listing?
50:10 - Ava Chen: yes, pilot can be done directly; marketplace listing is for CVM distribution. we can run the pilot while we prepare the marketplace artifacts.
52:00 - Carlos Mendes: small note, sometimes model names get munged in transcripts; you mentioned 'EdgeBound' earlier — just to confirm that's your internal codename for the offline offering?
53:12 - Daniel Park: yeah EdgeBound is our internal. public name will be VertexEdge.
54:30 - Priya Nair: going to call out a couple of technical risks: model quality regressions after quantization, and throughput variability on older CPUs. we'll run regression evals and include fallback to smaller seq lengths as a mitigation.
56:05 - Maya Singh: acceptable. make sure we have a rollback plan in the helm chart and that image tags are immutable for production.
57:30 - Carlos Mendes: helm chart will include imagePullPolicy and pinned digest references; we'll also add an example rollback script in the runbook.
59:00 - Ava Chen: okay let's recap next steps: i will share the packaging checklist and manifest example; carlos will deliver runbook and bench harness; priya will run an initial quant compatibility pass; vertexlynx will provision test vpc and provide SOC2 thumbnails. timeline dates are in action items. any final questions?
60:30 - Daniel Park: none from me, looks good, thanks all.
61:10 - Sofia Alvarez: thanks, we'll follow up on the compliance sync invite.
61:50 - Ava Chen: thanks everyone, we'll email the artifacts and next steps after the call.

References shared during call:
- Packaging checklist (link): /shared/vertexlynx-packaging-checklist.xlsx
- Helm example repo (link): https://git.internal.redwood/example-helm-vertexedge
- Lab runbook template (link): /labs/runbooks/vertex-edge-lab-runbook.md

Meeting closed.
